reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds to compare them with the handoff.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly: order 150, 151, and 155 with the same amounts. Next I'll list the orders to check that these refunds apply to real orders before computing balances.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is within its order's amount (150: 12682 of 18740, 151: 15870 of 25496, 155: 4209 of 18321). Next I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 9958 matches my check: orders 150 and 153 total 22640, minus the 12682 refund. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 42141 matches my check: orders 151 and 154 total 58011, minus the 15870 refund. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.
Alpha's refunds match the ledger, each refund is below its order amount, and all three net balances match my independent sums. I'll record acme's payout of 9958 first.
Acme's payout of 9958 recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 42141 matches my independent check (58011 minus 15870), so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net balance of 50848 matches my independent check: orders 152 and 155 total 55057, minus the 4209 refund for order 155. That was the last customer, so I'll record their payout.
All three customers have been paid. Each payout matched my independent check of order totals minus refunds, so the batch is complete.
